The Main Directorate of Intelligence of Ukraine's Ministry of Defence (HUR) has warned the military that Iran may launch at least three medium-range ballistic missiles from Tabriz in northwestern Iran against military infrastructure in Kyiv within the next 48 hours, in response to Ukraine's attack on an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea several days ago.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Ukraine's attack "cannot go unanswered."
Separately, several Ukrainian military-affiliated channels have also reported that Iran is preparing to launch ballistic missiles at targets in Ukraine, echoing the HUR warning.

A Ukrainian Navy officer's vehicle was targeted in an explosion this morning on Semen Palii Street in Odesa.
An explosive device had been placed beneath the front left wheel of the BMW X5 and detonated as the vehicle began moving.
The officer, identified as Viacheslav Sazonov, a senior officer in the Operations Department of the Logistics Directorate at the Headquarters of the Ukrainian Naval Forces Command, sustained only minor injuries due to the device's relatively small explosive yield.

Earlier today, the Iraqi Armed Forces shot down an unidentified unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) in the Muwailihah area, north of Babylon Governorate, southern Iraq.
There is considerable speculation regarding the UAV's identity, with some suggesting it could be a Chinese-made CH-4B or Wing Loong II operated by the Royal Saudi Air Force (RSAF).
However, the wreckage appears to show a 4-blade composite pusher propeller, whereas both the CH-4B and Wing Loong II are equipped with 3-blade pusher propellers.
Based on that detail, those two platforms seem unlikely. The only UAVs that come to mind with a 4-blade pusher propeller are the MQ-9B (SkyGuardian/SeaGuardian) and the MQ-9A Extended Range (ER).
The standard MQ-9A (Block 1/Block 5) uses a 3-blade propeller.
